hero.title: Soil Profile Of Uttar Pradesh
hero.description: The soil profile of Uttar Pradesh is primarily shaped by the Indo-Gangetic river system, varying from alluvial soils in the plains to red and mixed soils in the southern plateau. Understanding these agro-climatic zones, soil composition, and regional distribution is essential for clearing the Allahabad High Court RO/ARO and UPPSC examinations.

timeline.title: Chronological Evolution of Soil Mapping & Classification in UP
timeline.description: Key milestones in geological and agricultural soil mapping across Uttar Pradesh.

cards.details: Initial colonial land revenue surveys classified UP soils primarily based on irrigation availability (Chahi, Nahri) and texture (Bhur, Domat).
Systematic scientific classification divided Uttar Pradesh into distinct agro-climatic zones with dedicated soil testing frameworks.
Launch of nation-wide soil nutrient profiling to provide customized fertilizer recommendations to farmers across all UP districts.
Integration of GIS and remote sensing technologies for high-resolution district-wise soil degradation and nutrient mapping.

items.question: Which district of Uttar Pradesh has the maximum extent of Usar (saline-alkaline) soil?
items.answer: Aligarh and Mainpuri districts record some of the highest concentrations of saline-alkaline (Usar) soils in UP.

items.question: What is the local name given to the black cotton soil found in the Bundelkhand region of UP?
items.answer: 'Mar' and 'Kabar' are the local terms for heavy clay and black soils in the Bundelkhand region.

items.question: What chemical amendment is predominantly recommended for reclaiming alkaline (Usar) soils in Uttar Pradesh?
items.answer: Gypsum (Calcium Sulfate) is used to neutralize sodium carbonates in alkaline soils.

items.question: What distinguishes Khadar from Bhangar soils in the Gangetic plains of UP?
items.answer: Khadar is new alluvial soil replenished annually by floods and highly fertile, whereas Bhangar is old alluvial soil located at higher elevations containing kankar nodules.

traps.title: Common Exam Traps to Avoid
items: Alluvial Soil Fertility Myth: Aspirants often assume Alluvial soils are naturally rich in all nutrients. While high in potash and lime, UP alluvial soils are universally deficient in nitrogen and organic humus, requiring regular urea application.
Confusion between Mar and Rakar: Do not confuse 'Mar' (heavy, black, highly fertile clay soil of Bundelkhand) with 'Rakar' (sloping, eroded, less fertile red soil near hilly tracts of Bundelkhand).

sections.title: Major Soil Types and Classification in UP
sections.content:
Uttar Pradesh can be broadly divided into three major soil zones: Alluvial soils of the Gangetic plain, Southern Red and Mixed soils, and Vindhyan/Bundelkhand tract soils.

  • Alluvial Soil (Jallodh Mitti): Covers about 80% of UP's total land area, brought down by Himalayan rivers. Highly fertile, rich in potash and lime, but deficient in nitrogen and organic matter. Subdivided into Khadar (new alluvium) and Bhangar (old alluvium).
  • Khadar (New Alluvium): Found in floodplains of rivers like Ganga and Yamuna. It is sandy-clayey to loam in texture, replenished annually by floods, highly suitable for paddy, wheat, and sugarcane cultivation.
  • Bhangar (Old Alluvium): Found away from river floodplains at higher elevations. Contains kankar (calcareous nodules), less fertile than Khadar, requires intensive irrigation and fertilization.
  • Red and Mixed Soils (Lal Evam Mishra Mitti): Found in southern districts bordering Madhya Pradesh (Jhansi, Mirzapur, Sonbhadra, Banda, Chandauli). Formed due to weathering of ancient crystalline rocks. Rich in iron oxide (giving red color), poor in nitrogen, phosphorus, and humus.
  • Bundelkhand Tract Soils (Parwa, Mar, Kabar, Rakar): Specialized local soil classifications in the Bundelkhand region: 'Mar' is black cotton soil (clayey, sticky), 'Kabar' is heavy clay soil, 'Parwa' is sandy-loam (light soil), and 'Rakar' is sloping, eroded red soil found near hills.

sections.title: Soil Degradation, Salinity, and Reclamation in UP
sections.content:
Intensive farming, canal irrigation, and deforestation have led to severe issues like Usar (saline-alkaline) soils, ravine formation along Chambal, and soil erosion in the sub-Himalayan tract.

  • Usar / Alkaline Soils (Reh / Kallar): Extensively found in Aligarh, Mainpuri, Etawah, Unnao, Rae Bareli, and Kanpur districts. Characterized by high sodium carbonate/bicarbonate accumulation making soils impermeable and infertile.
  • Reclamation of Usar Soils: Gypsum (Calcium Sulfate) application is the primary chemical method used to replace sodium ions with calcium ions, followed by leaching and cultivation of salt-tolerant paddy varieties.
  • Ravine (Bihad) Formation: Caused by severe gully erosion by Yamuna and Chambal rivers in districts like Etawah, Jalaun, and Agra, turning fertile lands into rugged, undulating ravines.
  • Bhabhar and Terai Soil Erosion: Northern strip along the Nepal border faces heavy rainfall and rapid water runoff, causing sheet and rill erosion along with waterlogging in low-lying Terai pockets.
